findings.title: Relocating the active workspace re-lists the library before its sync state is detected
findings.body: For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` runs `relocateActive` (`switch-transaction.ts:100-141`). It calls `deps.afterCommit` and reopens the gate before it returns. `afterCommit` (index.ts:524-530) runs `broadcastState()` and `host.broadcastLibraryChanged()`. Only after that does line 755 call `syncStates.refresh(current)`. Until then `SyncStates.of` (`sync-state.ts:26-30`) sees that the stored path differs and falls back to the path rule, which only knows `~/Library/CloudStorage/...`. A Drive or iCloud folder that only the xattr check detects therefore looks unsynced: `availabilityOf` takes the unbounded `reg.availability` branch (line 179), `activeEvictionProbe()` returns null (line 369), `activeScratch()` returns null (line 375), and the `syncedStagingFor` check (line 397) is false. `refresh` can add up to 2 s (`SYNC_DETECT_TIMEOUT_MS`), and the app uses stale state for that long. A library re-list or a capture start in that window can read evicted files or stage a take in `.kaipu/tmp/` of the synced folder. The other branch (a non-active workspace) is not affected, because nothing re-lists for it. Consider detecting the new folder before the commit: call `syncStates.refresh({ id, path: chosen })` right after the picker returns, or inside the `apply` callback of `relocateActive`. The window then starts with the right state.

contracts.action: Change folder… (relocate): detect the new folder's sync provider, bound the availability probe, and return the workspace view
contracts.equivalent_path: addWorkspace (index.ts:577-612) and createWorkspace (index.ts:628-647) call `syncStates.refresh(entry)` and then `availabilityOf`, and return `toWorkspaceView(..., syncStates.of(entry))`. Startup does the same at line 115.
contracts.before_after: Add and create refresh sync state before any switch or broadcast, so the transaction sees the right state. Relocate refreshes only after `relocateWorkspace` returns. For the active workspace the transaction has by then already run `afterCommit` (broadcastState, broadcastLibraryChanged) and reopened the gate (`switch-transaction.ts:136`). For a non-active workspace the order is harmless, because no re-list happens.
contracts.visible_effect: The returned `workspace` view and the final `broadcastState` carry the correct sync provider and bounded availability, so the switcher shows the right sync badge. The `reg.get(...) ?? entry` fallback covers an entry changed during the dialog.
contracts.failure_mode: `detectSync` and `withTimeout` swallow errors and time out at 2 s (`synced-folder.ts:46-52, 22`), and `boundedProbe` limits the availability check to 5 s, so the IPC call cannot hang. A failed detection leaves the path-rule answer silently, with no visible state. The stale-state window for the active workspace is reported as a finding.

structuredOutput.summary: The only change in this part is that `relocateFolder` now detects the new folder's sync provider and bounds its availability probe. One finding, at "consider": when the active workspace is relocated, `afterCommit` re-lists the library before `syncStates.refresh` runs, so for up to about 2 s an xattr-detected synced folder is treated as unsynced. findings.title: Relocating the active workspace re-lists the library before its sync state is detected
findings.body: For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` runs `relocateActive` (`switch-transaction.ts:100-141`). It calls `deps.afterCommit` and reopens the gate before it returns. `afterCommit` (index.ts:524-530) runs `broadcastState()` and `host.broadcastLibraryChanged()`. Only after that does line 755 call `syncStates.refresh(current)`. Until then `SyncStates.of` (`sync-state.ts:26-30`) sees that the stored path differs and falls back to the path rule, which only knows `~/Library/CloudStorage/...`. A Drive or iCloud folder that only the xattr check detects therefore looks unsynced: `availabilityOf` takes the unbounded `reg.availability` branch (line 179), `activeEvictionProbe()` returns null (line 369), `activeScratch()` returns null (line 375), and the `syncedStagingFor` check (line 397) is false. `refresh` can add up to 2 s (`SYNC_DETECT_TIMEOUT_MS`), and the app uses stale state for that long. A library re-list or a capture start in that window can read evicted files or stage a take in `.kaipu/tmp/` of the synced folder. The other branch (a non-active workspace) is not affected, because nothing re-lists for it. Consider detecting the new folder before the commit: call `syncStates.refresh({ id, path: chosen })` right after the picker returns, or inside the `apply` callback of `relocateActive`. The window then starts with the right state.

contracts.action: Change folder… (relocate): detect the new folder's sync provider, bound the availability probe, and return the workspace view
contracts.equivalent_path: addWorkspace (index.ts:577-612) and createWorkspace (index.ts:628-647) call `syncStates.refresh(entry)` and then `availabilityOf`, and return `toWorkspaceView(..., syncStates.of(entry))`. Startup does the same at line 115.
contracts.before_after: Add and create refresh sync state before any switch or broadcast, so the transaction sees the right state. Relocate refreshes only after `relocateWorkspace` returns. For the active workspace the transaction has by then already run `afterCommit` (broadcastState, broadcastLibraryChanged) and reopened the gate (`switch-transaction.ts:136`). For a non-active workspace the order is harmless, because no re-list happens.
contracts.visible_effect: The returned `workspace` view and the final `broadcastState` carry the correct sync provider and bounded availability, so the switcher shows the right sync badge. The `reg.get(...) ?? entry` fallback covers an entry changed during the dialog.
contracts.failure_mode: `detectSync` and `withTimeout` swallow errors and time out at 2 s (`synced-folder.ts:46-52, 22`), and `boundedProbe` limits the availability check to 5 s, so the IPC call cannot hang. A failed detection leaves the path-rule answer silently, with no visible state. The stale-state window for the active workspace is reported as a finding.

structured_output.summary: The only change in this part is that `relocateFolder` now detects the new folder's sync provider and bounds its availability probe. It also returns the workspace view, matching what add and create already do. One finding, at "consider": when the active workspace is relocated, `afterCommit` re-lists the library before `syncStates.refresh` runs, so for up to about 2 s an xattr-detected synced folder is treated as unsynced. No open threads touch this file, so there are no thread replies.
